exposure: Secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure beginning on embryonic day 12.5 (SHS-6D)
Secondhand smoke (SHS) exposure beginning on embryonic day 14.5 (SHS-4D)
outcome: Levels of antibody-triggered complement activation pathway genes (C1QA, C1QB, C1QC)
Levels of collagen-related genes (COL1A1, COL4A5, COL4A6, COL17A1)
Levels of genes associated with cell-based lysis processes
cohort: Pregnant C57BL/6 mice were exposed to secondhand smoke via nose-only delivery starting on either embryonic day 12.5 or 14.5, continuing until E18.5, while control mice received ambient air.
finding: The timing of secondhand smoke exposure in pregnant mice results in unique patterns of placental gene regulation and involvement in biological pathways, with the SHS-4D group showing elevated inflammation and reduced complement activation, and the SHS-6D group exhibiting lowered expression of collagen-related genes.
gest_age: Exposure started on embryonic day 12.5 or 14.5, continuing up to E18.5.
